column1: # vdi-r3.tsv -- VDI reference dumper, round 3: effects, not echoes.
# Rounds 1 and 2 stay frozen with the dumps already measured. This is a
# separate table; a case id is a physical line number and the file CRC binds
# every dump to it.
# WHY THIS ROUND EXISTS
# Round 2 reached 112 of 120 green and still missed that vst_font (21) is an
# echo with no effect in NewTOS. Nothing in that table could have caught it:
# the runner resets before every case, so a set made in one case is gone by
# the next, and a case that reads a setter's echo proves only the echo.
# So this round is built on PRELUDES. A line whose opcode starts with '+' is
# a call issued after the reset and before the measured call, and is not
# recorded. Each pair below sets a NON-DEFAULT value and then reads it back
# through the matching inquiry. A default value would prove nothing, because
# a setter that does nothing at all leaves the default in place.
# Every opcode, sub-op and input arity is derived from the EmuTOS handlers,
# not written from memory: the jump tables (vdi/vdi_main.c:32-111), each
# handler's own INTIN[n]/PTSIN[n] reads, vsc_form's documented input list
# (vdi/vdi_mouse.c:502-509), and gdp_justified's INTIN[0]/[1] flags with the
# string from INTIN[2] and the count from CONTRL[3]-2 (vdi/vdi_text.c:1187).
# STILL NOT COVERED, and why
#   14 vs_color, 112 vsf_udpat   A prelude can set them, but the reset cannot
#                                undo them, so the state would leak into every
#                                later case. Covering them means extending the
#                                reset -- and the reset is part of the
#                                measurement contract: changing it would make
#                                this round incomparable with rounds 1 and 2
#                                and break the generated tests for those. It
#                                needs a versioned reset, which is its own
#                                task.
#   1, 2, 101                    Destroy the workstation the run measures
#                                through. Only 100 is here: it opens an
#                                ADDITIONAL virtual workstation without
#                                destroying ours, and returns the full 45-word
#                                DEV_TAB and 12-word SIZ_TAB -- which is where
#                                the SIZ_TAB fold bug of round 2 lived.
#   109, 110, 121                MFDB pointers in contrl[7..10] differ per
#                                machine; needs a comparison rule first.
#   118, 119, 120, 125-127, 134  Install vectors or change the global font
#                                ring; the reset cannot restore them.
#   124, 128                     Read the live mouse and keyboard. Not
#                                reproducible between two runs on one machine,
#                                which is the one thing a reference may not be.
# Appending only: a new case goes at the end.
# opcode
# --- line attributes: set non-default, read back via vql_attributes (35)
# --- marker attributes: read back via vqm_attributes (36) ------------
# --- fill attributes: read back via vqf_attributes (37) --------------
# --- text attributes: read back via vqt_attributes (38) --------------
